title: An option worse on every criterion never wins
why: Crest is cheaper and better than both others, and Bolt is pricier and worse than both.

title: Choosing a CRM vendor
why: Acme matches Cobalt on features at a lower price and beats Dynaforce on features and integrations; Evergreen is beaten by Acme on every criterion and Brightline is cheap but weak everywhere.

title: Three job offers with a salary floor
why: Nonprofit pays under the stated $100k minimum so it is off the list; the startup pays well, has the best growth and a short commute, while BigCorp's extra pay comes with a 50-minute commute and middling growth.

title: Apartment hunt where the dream loft is over budget
why: The loft is best on everything but rent, and rent is over the $2000 hard limit, so it is out however good it is; of the rest, Garden Flat has the best light, a decent size and a short commute at an affordable rent.

title: Kitchen remodel where one bid has no price
why: A missing price is unknown, not free, so QuickFix's weak reviews keep it from winning; Mason & Co is cheaper and faster than Hartley with nearly the same reviews.

title: Laptop shortlist with a strictly dominated model
why: Clone 14 costs more than Aero 14 and is worse on battery, weight and performance, so it can never be the right pick; Titan is heavy, pricey and short on battery, and Basic is cheap but weak.

title: Wedding venue where an absurd castle price sits in the column
why: With price weighted three times quality, the barn at about half the hotel's price for a modestly lower quality is the sensible pick; a castle nobody can afford should not change the barn-versus-hotel call (a divide-by-max price column lets it squash every real price difference to near zero).

ruling.winner: An outlier sets every scale it's in, ÷Max or Range alike (Range does worse here); the person's tool is a deal-breaker, which screens it before scaling: see wedding-venue-castle-capped.

title: The same venues with a budget cap: the castle is screened before it can bend the scale
why: Screened out before scaling, the castle no longer squashes the price column, and the barn's lower price wins as the weights say.

title: Vacation where Antarctica is unique but bad at everything else
why: Antarctica is the most unique trip but costs several times more, takes the longest to reach and is worst on weather and food; one standout criterion among five equally weighted ones shouldn't carry it.

title: Dinner spot where star ratings are bunched between 4.2 and 4.8
why: On review sites 4.8 against 4.2 is the gap between excellent and ordinary, and stars carry three times the weight of price, so the Range override should let Trattoria win; the diner wins only if stars are squashed by divide-by-max.

title: Used car with a mileage deal-breaker
why: The Accord's 128k miles break the 120k limit, so its low price can't buy it back; the Jetta is cheapest but has the worst reliability, which is weighted heavily.

title: Destination, then hotel, with a nightly-rate cap
why: Barcelona looks great on its own but every hotel there is over the $250 cap, so there is nowhere to stay; Lisbon has top weather, good activities, a cheaper flight and a well-rated hotel under the cap (its only one, as Reykjavik's only one is Harbor Lodge).

title: University, then program: prestige vs the program you'd attend
why: You attend a program, not a brand: Riverside's CS program is far better than anything at Ivy State and costs $14k less, which outweighs Ivy's reputation edge; Ivy Data Science beats Ivy CS on both faculty and placement.

title: Gym membership, then which branch, with a 5 km limit
why: FitMax is cheapest but has no branch within 5 km, so it's useless; Pulse is $10 cheaper than IronWorks with nearly as good equipment and a 24-hour branch 1.5 km away, the best branch on both counts.

title: City, then neighborhood, then apartment (three levels)
why: Denver has the best jobs but every apartment there is over the $2200 rent cap, so it falls out; Austin beats Portland on jobs with comparable neighborhoods, Mueller is safer and more walkable than East Riverside, and Sellwood is safer than Pearl with a much better apartment.

title: Two near-identical apartments: is the call fragile?
why: Maple wins only on slightly better light while Oak is cheaper and a bit larger, so a modest cut in Light's weight should hand it to Oak; both have laundry, so no weight on Laundry can separate them.

title: Dentist who is best on every count
why: Dr. Patel is soonest, best rated, closest and cheapest, so no weight on any criterion (short of flipping its sign) can make anyone else win.

title: Phone choice decided by a camera edge
why: Pixel edges Galaxy only through its camera while Galaxy is cheaper with a much better battery, so trimming the camera weight a little should flip the call to Galaxy.

title: Conference talks in a two-hour window
why: The 90-minute keynote is the best single talk but would leave room for only one more; four well-rated short talks fill the window far better, and the best of those comes first.

title: Project portfolio under a $500k budget with a prerequisite
why: The warehouse is dull alone but unlocks the dashboard, the most valuable project, and the pair plus the CRM upgrade fit in $450k; the mobile app would crowd out the dashboard pair, and the warehouse must be built first.

title: Grant round with at least two early-career awards
why: Two early-career awards are required, so fund the two best of those (Soil, Urban, $550k together) and then the best senior proposal that fits the remaining $450k, Quantum Sensors.

title: Five-man fantasy roster under a salary cap with position minimums
why: Keep the four stars (Jokic, Curry, Tatum, Brunson) and spend the last $7k on a second forward, which the position minimum demands even though a cheap guard or center projects slightly more; Hart is the only forward that fits.

title: Semester schedule with a time clash and a lab corequisite
why: ML and Databases meet at the same time, so take the more interesting ML; after ML and Statistics, the five remaining credits buy Physics I plus its very interesting one-credit lab, worth more than Art History alone.

title: Wedding vendors under $20k, one photographer and one caterer
why: The $12k gourmet caterer would eat the budget for flowers and music; the solid $7k caterer leaves room for the great photographer, the florist and the live band, a much better wedding overall.

title: Product roadmap ordered by value for engineering effort
why: With effort only a rough cost the answer is an order: CSV Export is a solid win for almost no effort so it goes first, and the Mobile App, valuable but ten times the effort of most items, belongs at the end.

title: Policy agenda spending rough political capital
why: The popular school lunch program earns goodwill rather than spending it, so it goes first and banks capital for the costly fights (carbon tax, pension reform) that come last.

title: Five-course menu with at least two vegetarian dishes
why: Two of five slots must be vegetarian, so take the two tastiest vegetarian dishes and fill the other three with the tastiest meat dishes.

title: Four investments under a total risk budget
why: The crypto fund's headline return uses most of the risk budget and leaves room for just one small holding; a diversified four of tech, index, REIT and dividends returns more in total within the same risk.

title: Hiring under a budget with a promised internal transfer
why: Dana was promised the job, so she's in first despite the weakest skill; the $270k left buys the best pair that fits, Alice and Chen.

title: Food tour where the top-rated spot is closed
why: Sushi Kaito is closed that day, so it can't be on the tour however good it is; the steakhouse alone would eat most of the $100, so four cheap, well-rated stops win.

title: One day in Paris: the Louvre vs a string of meh stops
why: A 10/10 must-see plus a lovely walk beats three below-average stops plus the walk; ratings of 4.5 are close to worthless, and adding three of them doesn't make one great experience.

ruling.plan: Summed scores treat a 4.5/10 as 45% of a 10/10, a true zero being nothing at all; whether a below-average stop is worth going to is the person's call, made with At least on Rating: see paris-day-minimum-rating. Range here would fix this one and break three other ladders.

title: One day in Paris, skipping anything below 6/10
why: With below-average stops ruled out, the day is the Louvre and the walk.

title: Menu that demands more vegetarian dishes than exist
why: Three vegetarian dishes are required but only two are on offer, so no menu can satisfy the brief; it should say so rather than return a plan.
